source.title: Data Mixing Can Induce Phase Transitions in Knowledge Acquisition
source.authors: Xin-Ran Gu; Kaifeng Lyu; Jia-Zheng Li; Jingzhao Zhang

record.tranche_reason: The study measures validation loss across model sizes and reports a fitted parameter-scaling function, using a different experimental setup from the original scaling-law studies. It also reports phase transitions in validation loss on knowledge-dense data mixtures.
record.gate_note: The fitted FineWeb-Edu validation-loss curve and the SynBio validation-loss phase-transition results bear directly on V1. The paper's accuracy, training-step, threshold-frequency, and threshold-popularity results are about knowledge acquisition rather than the loss behavior named by the versions; they are not recorded as rows. It does not test whether small-run loss fits predict much larger runs or whether a compute-optimal parameter/token split is stable.
record.test_reason: The paper's one loss-scaling result is a power-law fit of held-out FineWeb-Edu validation loss against parameter count (70M–410M Pythia, Fig. 7b). It is fitted only to calibrate the authors' threshold-frequency theory, so it is a weak test of V1 in a new data-mixture setting. Everything else measures knowledge acquisition (accuracy, threshold frequency) or per-domain SynBio loss, not the loss behaviour the versions name.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is mostly right but incomplete. The authors conclude that mixing knowledge-dense data into web data causes phase transitions in knowledge acquisition with respect to both model size and mixing ratio. They explain this with a capacity-allocation (knapsack) theory. Assuming web loss follows a power law in model size, they predict that the critical mixing ratio and threshold frequency follow power laws in model size, and validate this on synthetic biographies and PopQA. They also propose subsampling and compact knowledge mixing to improve acquisition at low mixing ratios.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses Pythia models and data mixtures, and fits one validation-loss relationship against model size; it does not reproduce the original studies' broader parameter, token, and compute scaling experiments or compute-optimal allocation analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: Validation-loss phase transitions are reported to depend on the knowledge-dense dataset and the varied setting: mixing ratio for Pythia-410M on SynBio-1.28M, and model size for Pythia models on SynBio-320k at r = 0.1.

fits_no_version.finding: Validation loss on a small knowledge-dense synthetic domain within a pretraining mixture changes sharply (a phase transition) with model size and with mixing ratio, rather than declining smoothly (Fig. 10a, b).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Per-domain loss on rare, knowledge-dense subsets of a data mixture can scale discontinuously with model size, even when aggregate web-data loss follows a power law.

record.problems: The directly relevant FineWeb-Edu loss fit covers only the stated 70M–410M model-size range and one validation dataset. The SynBio validation-loss phase-transition values are shown only in figures, without numerical values in the text. The authors state that computational costs prevented replication of all experiments with different random seeds.
record.rows_left_out: Knowledge-acquisition accuracy and training-step results, threshold-frequency/popularity results, and downstream-task results are omitted because they do not measure the validation-loss scaling, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Loss scaling with training tokens or compute; parameter scaling over several orders of magnitude; any check that data and compute were not bottlenecks.
All; downstream accuracy is reported only as a capability check for the mitigation strategies.

record.verdict_notes: The power-law web-loss scaling is mainly an assumption of the theory (Section 4.4 cites Kaplan and Hoffmann). The fitted exponent α ≈ 0.283 is used to predict a threshold-frequency slope of 1.283, against 1.152 observed. The study is not an original source. The extrapolation failure in Fig. 3c concerns training steps needed to reach a target accuracy, not loss, so it does not bear on V2.

versions.untested_parts: Tests validation loss against model size in the reported settings, but not loss scaling with training tokens or compute, nor the broad several-orders-of-magnitude regime with the other quantities established as non-bottlenecks.

rows.subject: Pythia models
rows.operation_detail: Fit validation loss on FineWeb-Edu as a function of model size.
rows.note: The paper reports this fitted function for the validation loss scaling with model size.
rows.check: The condition should state the training mixture: FineWeb-Edu mixed with SynBio-10k-power-law at r = 0.01 (Section 5.1, Fig. 7 caption). The fit spans under one order of magnitude (70M–410M). No goodness-of-fit or residuals are reported. The fit form (Hoffmann-style, with an irreducible term) is fixed by the authors' theory assumption.

rows.subject: Pythia-410M
rows.operation_detail: Vary the mixing ratio and measure validation loss on SynBio-1.28M.
rows.note: The text states that validation loss, a continuous metric, also shows phase transitions as the mixing ratio changes; no numerical values are given in the text.
rows.check: This row varies the mixing ratio, which is not parameters, tokens or compute. The loss is on the knowledge-dense SynBio domain only, not held-out pretraining loss as V1 names. Values are figure-only.

rows.subject: Pythia models
rows.operation_detail: Vary model size and measure validation loss on SynBio-320k.
rows.note: The text says the validation-loss phase transitions persist for this continuous metric; no numerical values are given in the text.
rows.check: This is per-domain loss on a tiny synthetic memorisation set inside the mixture, not overall held-out pretraining loss. It is better recorded under fits_no_version. Values are figure-only.

relationships.condition: Pythia 70M–410M trained on FineWeb-Edu mixed with 1% SynBio; FineWeb-Edu validation loss versus model size
relationships.reason: Loss fits L = 1.769 + 4.952·M^-0.283 (R1), but over under one decade and with no goodness-of-fit reported.
relationships.display_finding: Validation loss fitted L = 1.769 + 4.952·M^−0.283 over less than one decade of model size.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
